children: Hong Kong-listed shares of Bilibili rose sharply after reporting advertising revenue growth in the third quarter stayed resilient despite investor concerns.

The stock jumped as much as 15% to 95.70 Hong Kong dollars, equivalent to US$12.20, on Wednesday, before paring gains to trade 12% higher. The stock remains on track for its largest daily percentage gain since February last year.
Its American depository receipts closed 1.9% higher overnight.

The Chinese video-streaming platform posted adjusted net profit of 828.2 million yuan, equivalent to US$124.3 million, for the three months ended September, rising 5% from the same period a year ago. Its revenue rose 8% on year.
Citi analysts noted that the company's results were largely in line with consensus estimates.

In particular, Bilibili's third-quarter advertising revenue grew 20% on year. The segment had been a key concern for investors, as the company had highlighted pressure from macroeconomic conditions and poorer consumption in the second half of the year, the analysts said.

They reckon the segment's top-line growth remains on track toward hitting a mid-teen percentage in the fourth quarter, buoyed by users spending more time on the platform and rising advertising efficiency thanks to artificial intelligence.

Still, they expect Bilibili's adjusted operating profit in the fourth quarter to decline, given it faces a high base and likely lower games segment revenue. Citi trimmed its 2026 to 2028 earnings estimates by 2% to 5%.
Write to Megan Cheah at megan.cheah@wsj.com

title: Bilibili's Hong Kong-Listed Shares Surge Amid Resilient Advertising Growth
